Yuen Long attack incident seventh anniversary that day, Li Ying-chi holding a watermelon arrived at the scene, was stopped and searched by plainclothes police officers for nearly an hour, during which a folder with the words "搜乜撚嘢" written on it was found on her. Li Ying-chi, who works as a dentist at a non-profit organisation, said three days after the incident she suddenly received a call from the company requesting a meeting, and was asked to resign immediately, with the other party saying "asked me to be understanding of them, the organisation is big, if it doesn't do this, it will affect the whole organisation's cooperation with the government". Dismissed on the spot, she was unable to make arrangements for her patients in advance, believing the organisation's做法 was "reckless of patients' interests", and said "it will be hard for any organisation to hire me again", and would consider retiring.

On the day of 721, Li Ying-chi, holding a watermelon and a photo of the alleged attacker "Watermelon Man", went to Yuen Long Station, and was immediately taken by plainclothes police officers to a footbridge for a stop and search, during which a folder with "搜乜撚嘢" written on it was found, and she was only released after being detained for nearly an hour.

Told that "if it doesn't do this, it will affect the organisation's cooperation with the government"

She said that on the following Thursday (24 July), she suddenly received a call from the company asking her to come to the office for a meeting, and at that time she already sensed trouble. Upon arrival, a colleague who opened the door for her was in tears, "patted me, told me to take care". Subsequently, a colleague from the Human Resources Department met with her and asked if she would resign voluntarily, otherwise she would be dismissed; after she refused, she was dismissed immediately, "not even allowed to pack my things, colleagues will pack them up and mail them to me", "asked me to be understanding of them, the organisation is big, if it doesn't do this, it will affect the whole organisation's cooperation with the government".

Li Ying-chi quoted the other party as saying that she was convicted last year for unlicensed street fundraising, but had not declared it to the company. She admitted that she had not reported it because the case was unrelated to her profession, and was following up with the Dental Council, but there was no conclusion yet; she believed the nature of the case was minor and insufficient grounds for dismissal. The reason stated in the company's dismissal letter was ultimately unsatisfactory performances. Working two days a week, she asked herself whether she had ever received any patient complaints, and her performance and results were no worse than other dentists; she believed the organisation had "no real grounds, even if dissatisfied would not dismiss immediately, just cobbled together a reason", and that "the force behind it is unbelievable".

Reviewing the information, League of Social Democrats chairwoman Chan Po-ying, Yu Wai-bun, Chow Ka-fat, and Li Ying-chi set up street stations three times in Causeway Bay and Wan Chai in 2023, during which black cloth banners were hung, and they were summonsed for fundraising without approval. The four refused to plead guilty and were convicted after trial; Chan Po-ying was fined HK$6,600, while the other three were fined HK$1,000 to HK$3,000 each.

This year's 1 July, Li Ying-chi was followed by a large number of plainclothes police officers after arriving in Causeway Bay, and was then "escorted" to the MTR station to take a train and leave. (Information picture)

Li Ying-chi also revealed that this was the second time she had been immediately dismissed by an employer. She believed that the methods in both incidents were similar — both required her to "leave immediately, unable to handle the patients in hand" — and criticised this做法 as reckless of patients' interests. She said she had no difficulty finding a job after being dismissed last time, but "this time I'm prepared to lose", because many medical and non-profit organisations have cooperative relationships with the government, "if this is used as leverage, I won't be able to find work anywhere", and described the most regrettable thing as losing the opportunity to serve society. She said that in the long run she would consider retiring, because after working for many years she is "completely worn out"; in addition to occupational diseases, she also bears work pressure, describing it as "being sacked is actually one less worry".
